claims.text: OpenSecrets' series of contributions from pro-Israel PACs (PAC money only) runs from about $4.0M in 1990 to $2.1M in 2000, $5.1M in 2012, $5.9M in 2014, $7.5M in 2016, $8.7M in 2018 and $8.7M in 2020, a total of $71.3M for 1990–2020.

Cumulatively 1990–2020 the largest pro-Israel PACs were J Street PAC ($14.5M), NORPAC ($8.1M), National PAC ($4.5M), the Republican Jewish Coalition ($3.4M) and National Action Committee ($2.9M); J Street gave $4.2M in 2018 alone; Pro-Israel America PAC gave $905,889 and DMFI $337,135 in 2020.

The Washington Report on Middle East Affairs, from FEC data, reported pro-Israel PAC contributions to House and Senate candidates of $12,661,440 (2019–20), $17,175,455 (2021–22) and $44,656,374 (2023–24).

By the end of July 2024, per FEC data compiled by Sludge, AIPAC PAC had spent $44.8M ($42M to candidates, parties and leadership PACs, mostly earmarked individual donations) and UDP about $55.4M (more than $35M in independent expenditures), about $100.2M combined; AIPAC PAC had given Wesley Bell more than $3.1M.

The Guardian found pro-Israel donors had given over $58M to sitting members of Congress in their most recent elections, all but 33 members receiving some; the top six 2022 recipients, all centrist Democrats, received about $25M (about 42%); members supportive of Israel after 7 Oct 2023 averaged about $125,000 against about $18,000 for supporters of Palestinians; party, not money, predicted statements on civilian casualties.

Per FEC filings and OpenSecrets, 2022→2024 spending: AIPAC/UDP $44M→$95.1M; RJC and its super PAC $4.5M→$19.7M; J Street $8.6M→$14.6M; DMFI $7.7M→$4.8M; NORPAC $1.6M→$2.7M (fundraising events up from about 40 to 60 a year); Miriam Adelson gave the RJC super PAC $5M and was the largest individual donor to outside groups in 2024.
